candidate_reports.remark: The Glisson's Pond Fort Stewart RAWS site has measured 2.28 inches of rain since 7:34 am.
The Reidsville Airport (KRVJ) AWOS has measured 2.55 inches of rain since 7:15 am.
The Glennville UGA Weather Network site has measured 1.99 inches of rain so far today.
NWS Employee reported that Carolina Bay Drive is flooded_ but still passable in the down the middle of the road.
Emergency Manager reported that the intersection of Huger Street and King Street is closed due to flooding.
Emergency Manager reported that the intersection of Vanderhorst Street and Ogier Street is closed due to flooding.

A City of Charleston inundation sensor at the intersection of Huger Street and King Street measured a peak inundation of 1.78 feet. Flash flooding typically begins at this location when the inundation depth reaches 0.40 feet.
Mesonet station at the Citadel has reported 3.21 inches of rain over the past 3 hours_ with 1.45 inches in the past hour. Rainfall is ongoing.
Broadcast Media reported that the intersection of East Bay Street and Blake Street is flooded with an estimated 3-4 inches of water on the roadway.
CoCoRAHS spotter reports 4.91 inches of rainfall_ resulting in flooding. Rain is ongoing.
Emergency Manager reported that the portion of Morrison Drive located from East Bay Street to Highway 17 is closed due to flooding.
Emergency Manager reported that the intersection of Ashley Avenue and Bennett Street is closed due to flooding.
Emergency Manager reported that the intersection of Rutledge Avenue and Bennett Street are closed due to flooding.

Emergency Manager reported the intersection of Rutledge Avenue and Simons Street is closed due to flooding.
Emergency manager reports that Bull St between Ashley Ave and Halsey Blvd is closed.

Emergency manager reports that Calhoun St between Rutledge Ave to Smith St is closed.
Emergency Manager reported that the intersection of East Bay Street and South Market Street is closed due to flooding.
As of 1030 PM_ emergency officials had performed 9 water rescues with at least 20 cars underwater.

A City of Charleston inundation sensor at the intersection of Ogier Street and Calhoun Street measured a peak inundation of 1.58 feet. Flash flooding typically begins at this location when the inundation depth reaches 0.40 feet.

City of Charleston reported all lanes closed on Society Street at Washington Street due to saltwater flooding.
Emergency manager reported saltwater flooding on Church Street at Mill Street. Road was still open.
Saltwater flooding at the Highway 17 and Highway 61 split. Road is closed.

A maximum tide level of 7.41 ft MLLW (1.65 ft MHHW) was observed at the Charleston Harbor tide gage. Shallow Coastal Flooding typically begins along the coasts of Charleston and Colleton counties when tide levels reach 7.0 ft MLLW (1.24 ft MHHW) in the Charleston Harbor.

A maximum tide level of 7.21 ft MLLW (1.45 ft MHHW) was observed at the Charleston Harbor tide gage. Shallow Coastal Flooding typically begins along the coasts of Charleston and Colleton counties when tide levels reach 7.0 ft MLLW (1.24 ft MHHW) in the Charleston Harbor.
Broadcast media reported a road closure at Fishburne St and Hagood Ave due to coastal flooding.

A maximum tide level of 7.46 ft MLLW (1.70 ft MHHW) was observed at the Charleston Harbor tide gage. Shallow Coastal Flooding typically begins along the coasts of Charleston and Colleton counties when tide levels reach 7.0 ft MLLW (1.24 ft MHHW) in the Charleston Harbor.
Emergency manager reported road closed due to flooding on North and South Market Street between Meeting Street and Concord Street.
Emergency manager reported road closed due to flooding on North and South Market Street between Meeting Street and Concord Street.

A City of Charleston inundation sensor at the intersection of Ogier Street and Calhoun Street measured a peak inundation of. 0.67 feet. Flash flooding typically begins at this location when the inundation depth reaches 0.40 feet.
Emergency manager reported road closed due to flooding at the I-526 ramp on Sam Rittenburg BLVD.
Emergency manager reported road closed due to flooding at Windemere Boulevard and William Ackerman Lane.

A maximum tide level of 7.76 ft MLLW (2.00 ft MHHW) was observed at the Charleston Harbor tide gage. Moderate coastal flooding typically begins along the coasts of Charleston and Colleton counties when tide levels reach 7.5 ft MLLW (1.74 FT MHHW) in the Charleston Harbor.
Emergency manager reported road closed due to flooding on ramp from US 17 to SC 61.

A maximum tide level of 9.57 ft MLLW (2.07 ft MHHW) was observed at the Fort Pulaski tide gage located near the Savannah River Entrance. Shallow coastal flooding typically begins along much of the Georgia and far southern South Carolina coasts when tide levels reach 9.5 ft MLLW (2.0 ft MHHW) at Fort Pulaski.
St. John's Fire District reported flooding at Bohicket Marina.
